newsitem.title: UK: Syria accuses Israel of preparing for war.
newsitem.headline: Syria accuses Israel of preparing for war.

text.p: Syrian Foreign Affairs Minister Farouq al-Shara accused Israel on Wednesday of preparing for war by "refusing" to resume peace talks and by insisting it will not exchange land for peace.

"Building new settlements in the occupied territories is sufficient evidence that the Israeli government headed by (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu is not serious about peace at all," Shara told Britain's Channel Four News.
"On the contrary it is preparing for further tension, further violence, further wars in the Middle East."
Israel and Syria held sporadic peace talks over the last five years but never solved the problem of the Golan Heights, occupied by Israeli troops in June 1967 during the Six-Day War.
Israel's previous Labour government, ousted by hardliner Netanyahu in May elections, said it could make a partial withdrawal for full peace.

But Netanyahu has ruled out a Palestinian state or the return of occupied Arab land in exchange for peace. Talks scheduled to reach a final Israeli-Palestinian settlement have not resumed since Netanyahu took office.
Shara praised the Labour approach but said Israel was now "in fact preparing for war".

"Because if it refuses to resume the peace talks from the talks where they ended and if the Israeli government refuses to endorce the previous commitments and undertakings, then it is preparing for war."

He said Syria was committed to "just and comprehensive peace in the Middle East" but added: "No sane Israeli should expect that Syria would make peace with Israel without having back all its occupied territory."
Shara, who is in Britain seeking European Union support for peace efforts, added:

"What is important is that we now realise, both of us, that Netanyahu should not drive the region to another war. He should not miss the opportunity for making a comprehensive peace. If he misses this opportunity things will deteriorate. This deterioration is catastrophe is every sense of the word."
